E052-01.notes: Object of preposition 'of' in a relative clause needs 'whom'. 'who' is nominative; 'them' makes a comma splice / run-on inside the appositive ('many of them had paid' would need different punctuation); 'whose' requires a following noun.

E052-02.notes: A leaves 'Spending most of the 1940s on the problem.' as a fragment; B puts a fragment after a semicolon; C 'decided to build ... and spending' breaks parallelism (the participle has nothing to coordinate with). D attaches a participial phrase modifying Zamboni. Fact check: Zamboni worked on the idea from the early/mid 1940s and finished the Model A in 1949, so 'most of the 1940s' is acceptable.

E052-03.notes: 'His first successful model' is already uniquely identified, so the 'which' clause is nonrestrictive and needs paired commas. A has none; C and D have only one of the pair (C also separates nothing correctly before the verb, D puts a lone comma between subject and verb).

flags.note: Factual simplification: a Zamboni shaves the ice, collects the snow, washes/squeegees, and then lays down a thin layer of clean water to freeze; describing the third task as 'drying it' is slightly inaccurate (the machine resurfaces with fresh water rather than leaving the ice dry). Consider 'and laying down fresh water' or 'smoothing it with a new layer of water'. Does not affect the keyed answer.

E052-04.notes: Colon after an independent clause correctly introduces the list. B: semicolon before a non-clause list is wrong; C: 'such as:' puts a colon after an incomplete construction and 'such as' contradicts the exact count 'three'; D 'tasks that were shaving...' is wordy and awkward.

E052-05.notes: Only C quantifies the reduction (one driver vs. a crew; minutes vs. more than an hour), echoing sentence 3. A, B, D are vague. Fact: a resurfacing with the machine takes roughly 10-15 minutes, so 'in minutes' is supported.

E052-06.notes: Subject is singular 'Each'; 'of the rinks that bought a machine' is an intervening phrase. Past tense matches the narrative. C and D are plural and also shift tense.

E052-07.notes: 'regardless of who made it' clarifies that the name is applied to resurfacers made by other companies (genericized trademark). A, B, C are unsupported.

E052-08.notes: 'the figure skater Sonja Henie' is a restrictive appositive (the name identifies which figure skater), so no commas. B would treat the name as nonessential, implying only one figure skater exists; C and D separate with a single comma/dash that is never closed. Fact: Henie saw the machine at Iceland in 1950 and ordered two for her touring show, consistent with company history.

E052-09.notes: 'Within a few years' needs the 1950 anchor from sentence 8, and sentence 10's 'the rinks that bought a machine' depends on sentence 9 having introduced rinks placing orders. B loses the time anchor; C puts the effect before the orders; D separates it from the rink discussion and the conclusion.
